5:1 names Ananias and Sapphira; after Ananias’s death in 5:5–6, “his wife” in 5:7 is Sapphira’s relation to Ananias.
5:7 identifies the arriving wife as Sapphira; Peter asks her a question in 5:8 and “She said” identifies her answer.
5:8 names Sapphira in the conversation; Peter’s “her,” “you,” and “your husband” in 5:9 address her.
5:8–9 has Peter speaking to Sapphira; “his feet” in 5:10 are Peter’s feet. The verse itself names Ananias and Sapphira but not Peter.

The “we” in 5:32 continues the Peter-and-apostles answer begun in 5:29; Peter is expressly one of that speaking group.
5:34–39 gives Gamaliel’s counsel; “with him” in 5:40 refers to its named speaker, Gamaliel.
6:5 says Stephen was full of the Holy Spirit; 6:10’s “the Spirit” is the Spirit by whom Stephen speaks. The link is related because the phrase is not the full title/name.
6:9–10 names Stephen as the disputant; “him” whose words the witnesses claim to have heard in 6:11 is Stephen.
7:9 says God was with Joseph; 7:10 continues the subject God as the one who delivers Joseph and makes him governor.
7:54–56 is Stephen’s speech and scene; the “he” who looks up in 7:55 is Stephen, while God and Jesus are separately the figures he sees.
7:55 establishes Stephen as the subject; “and said” in 7:56 continues Stephen’s speech.
7:58–60 names Stephen and narrates his stoning/death; “his death” in 8:1 refers to Stephen.

8:14 names Peter and John as the men sent to Samaria; the “who” coming down and praying in 8:15 refers to them.
8:15 names the Holy Spirit; the subject “he” in 8:16 is that Spirit. “Christ Jesus” in the same verse is a separate direct mention.

8:14–15 sends Peter and John to Samaria and describes them praying; “they laid their hands” in 8:17 continues their action.

8:18–19 identifies Simon as the person offering money and speaking; Peter’s “you” in 8:20 addresses Simon.
8:20 addresses Simon; “you” and “your heart” in 8:21 continue that address.
8:20–21 is Peter’s address to Simon; “your wickedness” and “you” in 8:22 continue it.

8:26–35 follows Philip’s encounter with the Ethiopian; 8:36’s “they went on the way” includes Philip. The eunuch remains unnamed.
9:11 names Saul as praying; the vision’s “him” in 9:12 refers to Saul. The incoming Ananias is separately named and already mapped.
9:19–20 continues the account of Saul’s recovery and preaching; “Isn’t this he” and “he had come here” in 9:21 are Saul.
9:26 says Saul came to Jerusalem and 9:27 says Barnabas brought him to the apostles; “He was with them” in 9:28 is Saul.
9:28 continues Saul’s Jerusalem scene; “He spoke and disputed” in 9:29 is Saul.
9:26–29 describes Saul in Jerusalem; “him” brought to Caesarea and sent to Tarsus in 9:30 is Saul.

10:1 names Cornelius; the description and actions in 10:2 continue that same subject.
10:3 names Cornelius as the recipient of the vision; in 10:4 Cornelius asks “What is it?” The second “He said” is the unnamed angel, not Cornelius.
10:5 explicitly says “Simon, who is also called Peter”; “He is staying” in 10:6 refers to Peter, distinct from the tanner Simon named later in the verse.
10:7 names Cornelius as the one who called his servants and the soldier; “he sent them” in 10:8 continues Cornelius.
10:19 says Peter was pondering the vision; the Spirit’s “arise ... go with them” in 10:20 is addressed to Peter.
10:17–21 follows the messengers looking for Peter; in 10:22 they report that Cornelius was directed to invite “you,” meaning Peter.
10:23 says Peter set out with the messengers and Joppa brothers; “they entered Caesarea” in 10:24 includes Peter.
10:25–27 describes Peter entering and speaking with Cornelius; “He said to them” in 10:28 continues Peter as speaker.
10:24–30 establishes Cornelius and Peter as host and guest; “I sent to you” is Cornelius addressing Peter. Both candidates are named interlocutors.
10:24–30 establishes Cornelius and Peter as host and guest; “I sent to you” is Cornelius addressing Peter. Both candidates are named interlocutors.

10:39 says Jesus was killed; “God raised him up” in 10:40 refers to Jesus.
10:39–40 describes Jesus’ death and resurrection; “ate and drank with him after he rose” in 10:41 refers to Jesus.
10:40–41 describes Jesus raised and revealed to witnesses; “He commanded us” in 10:42 refers to the risen Jesus. The verse separately names God as the one who appointed him.

10:46–47 is Peter’s speech; “He commanded them” in 10:48 is Peter, and “they asked him” addresses Peter.

Festusは「I commanded him to be kept」と自身の指示を振り返る。Paulと皇帝称号のリンクに加えて、話者Festusをrelatedで結び付けるのが妥当。
